source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Protein intake has no relationship to healing because collagen formation does not require amino acids","B":"Protein is used only for skeletal muscle growth and has no meaningful role in wound repair","C":"Protein should be restricted for every client with a pressure injury regardless of other conditions","D":"Protein supports tissue repair and wound healing, and significant wounds can increase protein needs"}}
source_row.rationale: Adequate protein supports tissue repair, immune function, and wound healing. Nutrition plans for pressure injuries should be individualized, including consideration of increased protein needs when clinically appropriate.
